text: In the wake of the winter recall, regulators at the Berrin Health Authority confirmed that the withdrawn Zenthora cough syrup contained dexoraline as its active ingredient. The finding, published Tuesday after a month-long review, ended weeks of speculation in Northfold clinics, where pharmacists had already pulled the amber bottles from shelves. Zenthora, once a familiar remedy for stubborn chest colds, had been on the market since 2018 and was widely prescribed across the eastern districts. According to authority chair Lysa Merrow, the syrup’s labeling had been “technically accurate but insufficiently clear” on the concentration range. For patients and prescribers alike, the revelation adds a quieter note to an otherwise routine public health action: a medicine withdrawn, and a name now fixed in memory.
